changes.after: Add a file chooser and understand what it does before upload.

before: A file input lets a person choose local files deliberately. Selecting a file is not the same as uploading it. This exercise configures the markup only: it does not choose real personal files or contact an upload service.

type="file" requests a file chooser. multiple permits more than one chosen file. accept="image/png,image/jpeg" suggests image types to the chooser; it is not a trustworthy validation rule. name="photos" supplies the form field name. For a form sending files, method="post" with enctype="multipart/form-data" configures multipart encoding. action names a receiving route, which must actually be implemented.

```html

Choose PNG or JPEG photos you intend to share. Selection alone does not upload them.

``` There is no value containing a local path. A page cannot prefill an arbitrary local file selection by writing a path into the markup. Browsers may display a privacy-preserving fake path rather than a real filesystem location. A real receiving server must check size, content and authorization; filenames or accept hints are not sufficient. Do not activate Send on this example expecting a working service.

Build the optional labeled photos control, type hints, multiple selection and multipart POST configuration. Keep the visible explanation. Checks inspect attributes, not picker UI, file decoding or upload success. The supplied checks inspect markup or local form-data relationships; they do not submit a network request or certify a screen-reader or native-browser experience. Optional local practice: try the changed case in a disposable local page and explain the difference.
after: `type="file"` makes a file chooser. It lets a person pick a file from their device. In this form, choosing a file does not upload it. Uploading would happen when the form sends it to a receiving service.
`multiple` allows several files. `accept="image/png,image/jpeg"` suggests PNG and JPEG pictures in the chooser. It is a hint, not proof that the chosen files are valid pictures.

This form is set up to send chosen photos. ```html

Choose PNG or JPEG photos you intend to share. Selection alone does not upload them.

``` `name="photos"` names the file field. `method="post"` chooses how to send it. `enctype="multipart/form-data"` tells the browser to package the files and other values together. `action` names the receiving address. This practice does not include that service.

Build the shown form and labeled photos input. Keep the file optional, allow multiple files, and add the exact accept value. Connect the help paragraph with `aria-describedby`. Do not add a file path in a `value` attribute: a page cannot choose a local file that way. Run the checks; you do not need to choose or send any files.

before.question: Change accept to image/png. Does that prove every file reaching the server is a valid PNG?
choices: No. It is a chooser hint; the server still validates received files.
Yes, accept is a server-side content inspection rule.
Yes, multipart encoding converts every file to PNG.
before.explanation: accept guides selection, and multipart packages data. Neither verifies actual file contents or prevents altered requests.

after.question: Does accept="image/png" prove that every received file is a valid PNG picture?
choices: No. It guides the chooser; the receiving service still needs to check files.
Yes. It checks files on the receiving service.
Yes. It turns every file into a PNG.
after.explanation: `accept` suggests file types. It does not inspect every received file or convert its contents.
